Nuclear Waste Reprocessing Notes
WARNING! Only open it if you can neutralize nuclear waste! Stay clear of radiation sickness!

* Opening: pry the barrel open carefully with a crowbar, and make sure you deal with the fission products by chemical means only. Keep the opened barrel on your person; fission products do not pour out, and never should.
* Dissolution: add about 500 mL of concentrated acid. Keep acid above 98% of the non-radioactive liquid in the barrel.
* Valence adjustment: once dissolved, add about 20 mL of reducing agent.
* Extraction: pour in ethyl acetate, at least twice the fission products, about 100 mL. Add all 100 mL at once to extract as much plutonium as possible.
* Separation: pour the barrel into a clean container. Only the plutonium extract and volatile liquids come out; acid and impurities stay in the barrel.
* Plutonium: heat the liquid above 100 C to drive off water, organics and alcohol.

* Vitrification: once the barrel is emptied, decay heat takes it above 300 C. Add 50 mL of water glass; the fission products melt into glass, sealed in a steel canister, and can be disposed of safely.
* Protection: never spend the night with unprocessed waste, or you will catch radiation sickness that only Immunivax can cure.
* Plutonium ampoule: pure plutonium solution can be filled into plutonium ampoules in the Chem Finisher. Add one to any drink or wine to make a nuclear drink worth 50 credits more.

Brine Electrolysis Notes

- Rock salt ore: order it from GP Mining by phone (6 in 1 day; 12 in 2 days once you have spent 350 there). Any blender crushes it into about 80 mL of salt plus a little clay and mineral; fewer chem modules lose more
- Electrolyzer: sold by Dr. Jackson with two empty gas canisters. Battery on the left, brine container in the middle, product A (hydrogen) top right, product B (chlorine) bottom right

- Each night it electrolyses 240 mL of salt (more with performance): every mL of salt uses 0.3 mL of water and leaves 1 mL of base in the container, plus 0.5 mL each of hydrogen and chlorine. It stops without salt, water, power or canister room. Efficiency saves power; quality from -100 to +100 scales the products from half to one and a half
- Filter the clay and mineral out of the base with a water filter, and boil off extra water in the evaporator
- Mixing: drag the chlorine canister onto the hydrogen canister (or the other way round); the gas moves into the target, and what does not fit stays behind
- Burning: put the mixed canister on a heating plate and heat it past 120 C (the plate needs at least 1 chem module); hydrogen and chlorine burn 1:1 into twice the volume of hydrogen chloride

- Dissolving: drag the hydrogen chloride canister onto a container with water; it dissolves into acid up to 40% of the liquid (500 mL of water takes at most 333 mL of acid), and the rest stays in the canister. For weaker acid, measure out the strong acid with droppers or cylinders and add water
- Do not pour hydrogen chloride into a container that still holds base: the base neutralizes the acid
- A canister holds 5 L; right-click to vent it. The retired chemist sometimes sells empty canisters
Incapacitant Production Notes
- The retired farmer sells Hollow's Lantern seeds. Annual, gives one seed back at harvest; hungry for nutrients, and its roots foul the water
- Blend the chilis: you get capsaicin only, no water or protein

- Heat above 50 C: capsaicin turns into Lantern Ester, using 0.1 part alcohol per part capsaicin. Alcohol boils at 78 C and burns off above that, so keep it at 50-78 C
- Filter out the physical contaminant, then dry off the alcohol in the evaporator. Unreacted capsaicin stays behind and lowers purity
